Super Spike.reasoning: Hormuz effectively CLOSED (only 16.8 mb/d vs 21 normal), Iran production completely offline (5.4 mb/d), Saudi/Kuwait major disruptions (3.7 mb/d combined). Total ~47 mb/d at risk per today reports. Escalation score 8/10 with active naval combat and missile strikes. Front-month CL volatility at 91% signals extreme market fear of supply collapse. Fitch cutting global growth to 2.4% confirms macro impact. This IS the super spike scenario manifesting.

Major Disruption.reasoning: Alternative view: Hormuz still passing SOME oil (16.8 mb/d), suggesting not total closure. Suez rerouting working. Kazakhstan ramping alternative supply. If current state stabilizes without further escalation, we remain in major disruption (130-180 range) rather than full super spike. Market volatility could be fear-premium, not reality.

Moderate Escalation.reasoning: Significantly reduced probability. Data contradicts moderate scenario: Iran production at ZERO, Hormuz down 20%, escalation score 8/10, active combat. We are well beyond limited strikes territory. Only plausible if viewing this as temporary peak before stabilization.

Current State.reasoning: Nearly impossible. 47 mb/d supply at risk, Iran completely offline, Hormuz partially blocked, severity 9.3/10 shipment disruptions, CL vol at 91%. This is categorically NOT a contained conflict with minimal supply impact. Market has clearly moved past this scenario.

De-escalation.reasoning: Minimal probability. No ceasefire signals, active naval combat in Persian Gulf, IRGC launching missiles at Israel. Escalation score 8/10 indicates worsening not improving. US inflation hitting 3-year highs creates domestic pressure but no visible diplomatic progress. Events moving opposite direction.

Resolution.reasoning: Essentially zero near-term probability. War actively intensifying with infrastructure warfare, complete Iranian production shutdown, and Hormuz blockade. No peace talks visible. Would require dramatic policy shift not evidenced in current intelligence. Australia sourcing oil from unlikely places signals long-war expectations.

overall_assessment: We are IN a Super Spike scenario: Hormuz effectively closed (80% capacity loss), Iranian production completely offline, 9+ mb/d total disruptions, escalation score 8/10 with active combat. The only question is whether this stabilizes at Major Disruption or deteriorates further into full crisis.
